title: ActiveRecord
body:
Rails' object-relational mapper: database tables are exposed as Ruby classes and rows as objects, so `Review.where(rating: 5)` generates the [[SQL]] instead of you writing it. It's an implementation of the Active Record pattern, where the object itself carries both its data and the methods to persist it.

The upside is a lot less boilerplate and a schema that reads as ordinary application code, with associations (`has_many :reviews`) turning [[Foreign Key]] relationships into method calls. The classic downside is the **N+1 query problem**: looping over records and touching an association inside the loop silently fires one query per record, which is why eager loading exists. This all runs on the app server; the queries it emits execute on the database server. Schema is evolved with [[Database Migration]]s.
